title: Bind SQLite catalog relationships using SQLite identifier semantics
applies_when: A SQLite schema inspector groups trigger or index catalog rows by table name and compares them with table definitions, especially when CREATE TABLE and ON target spellings differ in ASCII case.
lesson: Related sqlite_schema text fields need not have identical spelling even when SQLite resolves them to the same object. Records and ON records can identify one table while tbl_name retains the target spelling; an exact-string map silently omits its triggers. Resolve the relationship to the table's catalog spelling with SQLite's built-in ASCII NOCASE comparison, and use the same comparison in fallback queries. Preserve explicit main-schema selection so temp objects cannot redirect inspection. Test clean, missing, changed and extra triggers, PRAGMA-shadow fallback, and non-ASCII-distinct tables. After upstream refactors, review both optimized and fallback producer/consumer paths and retain query-count guards rather than mechanically taking either conflict side.
avoid_when: Built-in NOCASE is not Unicode case folding: JavaScript toLowerCase can merge identifiers SQLite keeps separate. Application data may require binary, locale-specific, ICU or custom collation rules; this lesson does not choose them. Native schema-owner tests do not establish full Doctor/update workflow, concurrency, all-platform or performance qualification.

evidence.note: Official documentation defines built-in NOCASE as folding only the 26 ASCII uppercase letters, not general Unicode normalization.
Submitted schema-owner repair joins trigger targets to table catalog spelling using NOCASE; the separate fallback query follows the same rule. Not evidence of merge or full-workflow success.

Registered tests cover clean/missing/drifted/extra triggers, ASCII target spellings, PRAGMA-shadow fallback, cached/uncached connections, non-ASCII-distinct tables and the upstream metadata-query-count guard.

Exact-head conflict refresh records native Linux Node 24.16 owner proof: 117 passes, 2 existing version-related skips, and 10 expected current-main regression failures with unchanged tests and dependencies. Prepared private dependencies were reused; hosted CI installation failed before tests on HTTP 503. Not full-package or all-platform proof.
